observations.why: Present-continuous 'we're switching' performs a settled, load-bearing commitment the speaker expects others to act on — ratification language, not a proposal being argued for.
Flat unhedged assertions presented as justification — asserted and ready to defend, but these are supporting arguments for a decision, not the decision itself; no ratification language present.
The arrow notation performs the migration as a settled plan item with a timeline — formatted as an operational directive, not a proposal under discussion.
